summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would make minor and technical corrections to Commonwealth laws and remove outdated Acts.
Schedule 1 would fix errors, update references, and delete spent provisions in various Acts.
Schedule 2 would repeal obsolete Acts without affecting any rights or obligations that arose under them.
changes: Corrects errors and updates references in Commonwealth Acts.
Removes spent or redundant provisions from the statute book.
Repeals obsolete Acts without affecting past actions or legal rights.
summary.affected: Commonwealth departments and agencies, and persons with rights or obligations under the repealed Acts.

speeches.speaker: Michelle Rowland
speeches.brief: Moved the second reading of the Statute Update Bill 2026, which makes minor technical amendments to 42 Commonwealth acts and repeals 106 spent or obsolete acts. Reported that the measures correct errors, update references, improve readability and reflect modern drafting practice without changing, or only minimally changing, the substance of the law.

speeches.speaker: Tony Burke
speeches.brief: Declared that, unless otherwise ordered, the Defence Legislation Amendment (RCDVS Implementation and Related Measures No. 2) Bill and the Statute Update Bill stood referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration after adjournment of their second-reading debates.

speeches.speaker: Zoe McKenzie
speeches.brief: Supported the Statute Update Bill's technical corrections, terminology updates, repeals and cross-reference changes, but sought referral to the Senate Legal and Constitutional Affairs Legislation Committee. Asked that the committee verify amendments affecting veterans legislation, the Criminal Code, family law and other areas do not create substantive changes to rights, obligations or entitlements.

speeches.speaker: Tom French
speeches.brief: Supported the Statute Update Bill 2026 as technical legislative maintenance, covering amendments to 42 Commonwealth acts, repeal of 106 spent or obsolete acts, corrected references and modernised communication provisions; noted the bill's non-contentious purpose, no financial impact and compatibility with human rights, while seeking clear explanations of veterans' indexation changes and payments.
